security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from PostgreSQL documentation examples, generated prose, and markdown fences. The only confirmed issue is the oversized references/sql.md file that was not fully covered by static scanning. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Oversized reference file skipped by static scanning
remediation.suggestion: Split references/sql.md into smaller topic files or provide a scanned index so automated review covers the whole reference set.

remediation.issue: Generated one-line excerpts in SKILL.md trigger obfuscation heuristics
remediation.suggestion: Wrap generated documentation excerpts to normal line lengths and keep long API text in reference files.

remediation.issue: Administrative shell examples appear in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Label privilege-changing commands as manual PostgreSQL installation examples and remind users to review them before running.

content.value_statement: PostgreSQL questions often span SQL syntax, schema design, and operations. This skill provides focused answers from bundled PostgreSQL reference material.
actual_capabilities: Explains PostgreSQL SQL syntax and query behavior from bundled references.
Guides schema design topics such as indexes, constraints, transactions, and data types.
Summarizes administration topics including installation, roles, authentication, and configuration.
Provides libpq connection string and client API reference context.
Helps interpret PostgreSQL examples and common error messages from the included documentation.
limitations: It does not connect to databases or execute SQL by itself.
The bundled references may lag the newest PostgreSQL release.
Generated excerpts in SKILL.md are dense and should be checked against reference files.
It does not replace production DBA review for migrations or security changes.

use_cases.title: Design a Reliable Schema
use_cases.description: Use PostgreSQL references to compare data types, constraints, indexes, and transaction behavior before implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan Database Operations
use_cases.description: Review installation, authentication, roles, configuration, and maintenance topics before changing a PostgreSQL environment.

use_cases.title: Debug Query Behavior
use_cases.description: Clarify SQL clauses, joins, window functions, and error messages while building reports or pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Learn Core SQL
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the PostgreSQL concepts behind SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, and HAVING. Use simple examples and note common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Table
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PostgreSQL table design goals. Recommend data types, constraints, and indexes, and explain each tradeoff.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a Slow Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me analyze why a PostgreSQL query may be slow. Focus on indexes, joins, planner behavior, and safe next checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Secure Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PostgreSQL operations checklist for roles, authentication, connection settings, backups, and release-sensitive configuration changes.

output_examples.input: I need to understand why HAVING is different from WHERE.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that WHERE filters rows before grouping, while HAVING filters grouped results after aggregates are calculated.

output_examples.input: I need a local PostgreSQL connection strategy for development.
output_examples.output: The skill compares URI and keyword connection formats, then explains host, port, database, user, and timeout considerations.

output_examples.input: I need to choose indexes for a frequently filtered table.
output_examples.output: The skill describes when indexes help, why selectivity matters, and why unused indexes add write overhead.

best_practices: Check the detailed reference file when an answer depends on a PostgreSQL release or exact syntax.
Ask for tradeoffs when changing indexes, authentication, roles, or storage settings.
Validate generated database guidance in a staging environment before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not run administrative shell commands from examples without reviewing paths, users, and privileges.
Do not paste production secrets, connection strings, or private keys into prompts.
Do not treat general documentation guidance as a substitute for migration testing.

faq.question: Does this skill run PostgreSQL commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference-based guidance and does not execute SQL or shell commands.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with performance tuning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain indexes, query planning topics, and configuration concepts from the bundled references.

faq.question: Can it replace a database administrator?
faq.answer: No. Production changes still need review, backups, staging tests, and operational approval.

faq.question: Why are there security warnings in the audit?
faq.answer: Many warnings come from documentation examples, long generated lines, and administrative command text.

faq.question: Is the bundled SQL reference fully scanned?
faq.answer: No. The large SQL reference exceeded static scanner limits and should be split for complete automated review.
